headline.summary_title: A quiet tape with energy doing all the work
headline.intro_sentence: The S&P 500 added 0.33% and no major benchmark moved more than 1.4% in either direction. Cooler July inflation took the front end lower, but the 30-year auction cleared at its highest yield since 2001 and crude rose 5.36% on the Hormuz deadlock; our tactical allocation stays neutral equities, underweight fixed income, overweight cash, gold and commodities.

three_observations.headline: Energy is carrying the year
three_observations.body: It was the only sector up more than 2% on the week and, at +37.80% year to date, is more than fourteen points ahead of the next-best sector.

three_observations.headline: The scoreboard flatters the tape
three_observations.body: Core bonds ended barely positive at +0.13% after a full round trip, and the Aggregate is up just 0.04% on the year.

three_observations.headline: Breadth is still where the returns are
three_observations.body: The Russell 2000 leads at +23.46% year to date and MSCI EM, at +1.38%, led the week.

four_drivers.policy_note: On the policy side: June CPI fell 0.4% m/m (annual rate down from 4.2% to 3.5%) and July hike odds collapsed from 42% to 17%, but Chair Warsh stayed firm on inflation.
four_drivers.intro_sentence: Cooler inflation took the front end lower, the long end would not follow, energy stayed bid on the Hormuz deadlock, and the consumer is visibly cooling.

drivers.title: Cooler inflation, at last
drivers.body: July CPI confirmed US consumer inflation is cooling, headline easing to 3.4% and core to 2.5%, though annual producer inflation is still 4.7% headline and 4.2% core.

drivers.title: The long end would not cooperate
drivers.body: Cooler prints rallied Treasuries mid-week; Thursday's auctions took it back. The 30-year cleared at its highest yield since 2001.

drivers.title: Hormuz kept a bid under energy
drivers.body: Oil traded 85-89 USD/bbl and rose 5.36% as the deadlock held and the IEA projected the widest global supply deficit in five years.

drivers.title: A consumer that is cooling
drivers.body: Retail sales fell 0.6% month on month against a 0.1% rise expected, with no growth in real worker compensation in Q2.

scenario.intro_sentence: The house baseline is a resilient global recovery, 'Indian Summer for 2026' at 50% probability, balanced against a 30% inflation-heatwave and a 20% growth-freeze risk scenario.

house_view.intro_sentence: The weight of the evidence leads us to stay neutral on equities, cash is overweight, and we maintain an overall underweight stance on fixed income; in alternatives we stay overweight gold and commodities.

views.body: We stay neutral equities. Solid earnings growth, resilient activity and healthy consumer spending continue to support the asset class, and technicals remain positive.
We keep an overall underweight stance on fixed income. Fiscal deficits, treasury supply and duration risk argue for keeping the underweight for supply reasons rather than policy reasons.
We stay overweight gold and commodities as policy hedges, and cash is overweight; all currencies are underweight against the US dollar, but the yen stays neutral.
